chunks.heading: 4. Dismantling and assembly
chunks.text: Dismantling and assembly

chunks.heading: Position numbers
chunks.text: Position numbers Position numbers of parts (digits) refer to exploded views, sectional drawings and parts lists; position numbers of tools (letters) refer to 3. Service tools.

chunks.heading: Before dismantling
chunks.text: Before dismantling Disconnect the electricity supply to the motor. Close the isolating valves, if fitted, to avoid draining the system. Remove the electric cable in accordance with local regulations. Note the centre of gravity of the pump to prevent it from overturning. This is especially important in the case of long pumps.

chunks.heading: Before assembly
chunks.text: Before assembly Gaskets and O-rings should always be replaced when the pump is overhauled. Clean and check all parts. Order the necessary service kits. Replace defective parts by new parts.

chunks.heading: During assembly
chunks.text: During assembly Lubricate and tighten screws and nuts to the torque stated. See 2. Tightening torques and lubricants. 7 / 20

chunks.heading: 4.1.1 Fitting the transport bracket
chunks.text: 4.1.1 Fitting the transport bracket Press home the shaft (pos. 51). Press home the driver of the shaft seal (pos. 105) and tighten the three screws (pos. 113). Lift the shaft (pos. 51) and fit the adjusting fork. Fit the coupling (pos. 8) and the screws (pos. 9), but leave loose. Fit the transport bracket (pos. 700) or (pos. 701 and 702). Fit the two screws and nuts (pos. 703 and 704), but leave loose. Tighten the screws (pos. 9) in the coupling. The coupling must be fitted so that it is possible to remove it without slackening the screws (pos. 703). Tighten the screws (pos. 703). Remove the adjusting fork. The pump can now be transported without motor. 8 / 20

chunks.heading: 4.1.2 Removing the transport bracket
chunks.text: 4.1.2 Removing the transport bracket It is very important to proceed according to these instructions, as the shaft seal may otherwise be damaged. Remove three of the screws (pos. 9). Slacken the last screw (pos. 9), but do not unscrew it completely. Hit the end of the hexagon key carefully with the flat of the hand to loosen one of the coupling halves. Remove the last screw (pos. 9) and the loose coupling half. Hit the flat part of the coupling half on the shaft end very carefully. Remove the coupling half when it is loose. Remove the screws (pos. 703) and the nuts (pos. 704) and remove the transport bracket. Slacken the screws (pos. 113) by 1/4 turn. Lift the shaft (pos. 51) and fit the adjusting fork. Tighten the screws (pos. 113) with 2.5 Nm. Fit the motor to the pump head. Fit the screw (pos. 28), lubricate and tighten them diagonally to the torque stated. See 2. Tightening torques and lubricants. Fit the pin (pos. 10) and the two coupling halves (pos. 10a). Lubricate the four screws (pos. 9) with Thread-Eze and fit them. Yellow-chromated couplings: Check that the gaps either side of the coupling halves are equal. Fig. 3 Gaps between coupling hal v es

chunks.heading: 4.1.2 Removing the transport bracket
chunks.text: Tighten the screws (pos. 9) to the torque stated, see 2. Tightening torques and lubricants, and remove the adjusting fork. Check that the shaft rotates freely and noiselessly. Place the adjusting fork on the inside of one of the coupling guards. Fit the coupling guards (pos. 7) and the screws (pos. 7a). 9 / 20

chunks.heading: 4.2 Dismantling the pump
chunks.text: 4.2 Dismantling the pump

chunks.heading: 4.2.1 Removing the motor, coupling and shaft seal
chunks.text: 4.2.1 Removing the motor, coupling and shaft seal Remove the screws (pos. 7a) together with the coupling guards (pos. 7). Remove the screws (pos. 9) together with the coupling halves (pos. 10a) and the shaft pin (pos. 10). Remove the screws (pos. 28). Lift the motor off the pump head (pos. 2). Slacken the three screws of the shaft seal (pos. 113) by approx. ¼ of a turn. Slacken the shaft seal (pos. 105) using the ring insert tool for shaft seal (pos. B) until the thread is completely free of the pump head. Pull the shaft seal off the shaft.

chunks.heading: 4.2.2 Dismantling the pump main parts
chunks.text: 4.2.2 Dismantling the pump main parts Remove the shaft seal. See 4.2.1 Removing the motor, coupling and shaft seal. Remove the nuts (pos. 36) together with the washers (pos. 66a). Loosen the pump head (pos. 2) with a light knock on the edge and lift it free of the staybolts (pos. 26). Remove the outer sleeve (pos. 55). Lift the chamber stack off the base. Remove the O-rings (pos. 37).

chunks.heading: 4.2.3 Dismantling the chamber stack
chunks.text: 4.2.3 Dismantling the chamber stack Dismantle the pump main parts. See 4.2.2 Dismantling the pump main parts. Place the shaft holder (pos. A) in a vice, but do not tighten the vice. Fit the shaft pin (pos. 10) into the shaft pin hole, place the chamber stack in the shaft holder (pos. A) and tighten the vice. Fig. 4 Fitting the chamber stack in the holder Remove the screws (pos. 26b) and the washers (pos. 26c) holding the straps to the chamber stack. Remove the straps (pos. 26a) and the inlet parts (pos. 44b) and 44a. Remove the nut (pos. 67), the washer (pos. 66) and the splined clamp (pos. 64c). Remove the chamber stack parts: impellers, spacing pipes, chambers and bearing rings. See 5. Order of assembly of chambers and impellers. Remove the driver (pos. 61). If the neck rings (pos. 45) in the chambers are worn, remove them by pressing off the retainer for neck rings using the puller for neck ring (pos. C). CR 15 and 20: If the wear rings of the impellers (pos. 49c) are worn, remove them with the puller for neck ring (pos. C). 10 / 20

chunks.heading: 4.3 Assembly
chunks.text: 4.3 Assembly

chunks.heading: 4.3.1 Assembling the chamber stack
chunks.text: 4.3.1 Assembling the chamber stack Fit the neck rings into the chambers (pos. 45) if removed. CR 15 and 20: Fit the wear rings on the impellers (pos. 49c) if removed. Place the shaft holder (pos. A) in a vice, but do not tighten the vice. Fit the shaft pin (pos. 10) into the shaft pin hole, place the chamber stack in the shaft holder and tighten the vice. Check that the lock ring of the shaft (pos. 51) is not damaged. Fit the driver (pos. 61). Fit the chamber stack parts on the shaft: chamber, spacing pipe, impeller and bearing ring. See 5. Order of assembly of chambers and impellers. Note: When fitting the chamber stack make sure that bearings and other rotating parts are not dropped on the shaft. They must be slid carefully over the shaft to prevent any damage to bearings. Fit the splined clamp (pos. 64c), washer (pos. 66) and nut (pos. 67) and tighten with 22 Nm. Note: The washer (pos. 66) consists of two washers glued together. If they have been separated, make sure that they are fitted correctly. It is advisable to replace the washer (pos. 66) and nut (pos. 67) each time the chamber stack is dismantled. Fig. 5 Correct fitting of washer (pos. 66)

chunks.heading: 4.3.1 Assembling the chamber stack
chunks.text: Fit the inlet parts (pos. 44a and 44b) and the straps (pos. 26a). Fit the washers (pos. 26c) and the screws (pos. 26b) holding the straps to the chamber stack. Check that the straps are straight (parallel with the shaft), and tighten the screws alternately to ensure that the chamber stack is clamped straight. Tighten with 15 Nm. Slacken the vice and remove the chamber stack (pos. 80) and the shaft pin (pos. 10).

chunks.heading: 4.3.2 Fitting the pump main parts
chunks.text: 4.3.2 Fitting the pump main parts Assemble the chamber stack. See 4.3.1 Assembling the chamber stack. Fit the O-ring (pos. 37) in the pump head (pos. 2) and in the base (pos. 6) and lubricate them with Rocol 22. Fit the chamber stack on the base taking care that the heads of the screws for straps do not touch the inlet pipe in the base. Fit the outer sleeve (pos. 55) in the base and press it home in the base. Check that the four rubber springs (pos. 60) are in the pump head. Fit the pump head on the pump with the air vent screw (pos. 18) towards the discharge side. Lubricate the threads of the staybolts (pos. 26). See 2. Tightening torques and lubricants. Fit the washers (pos. 66a) and the nuts (pos. 36). Tighten the nuts (pos. 36) diagonally to the torque stated. See 2. Tightening torques and lubricants. 11 / 20

chunks.heading: 4.3.3 Fitting the shaft seal, coupling and motor
chunks.text: 4.3.3 Fitting the shaft seal, coupling and motor Fit the pump main parts. See 4.3.2 Fitting the pump main parts. If necessary, clean and smooth the shaft end using the holder with emery cloth supplied with the shaft seal kit. Moisten the shaft end with soapy water. Press the shaft seal on the shaft, screw it into the pump head and tighten it with 35 Nm using the ring insert tool for shaft seal (pos. B). Press the ring with the three set screws (pos. 113) against the hexagon plug. Tighten the screws (pos. 113) with 2.5 Nm. Lift the chamber stack by inserting a screwdriver or similar tool in the hole for the pin in the shaft and fit the adjusting fork, which is fitted to one of the coupling guards (pos. 7). TM02 7923 4403 Fig. 6 Fitting the adjusting fork Fit the motor to the pump head. Fit the screw (pos. 28), lubricate and tighten them diagonally to the torque stated. See 2. Tightening torques and lubricants. Fit the pin (pos. 10) and the two coupling halves (pos. 10a). Lubricate the four screws (pos. 9) with Thread-Eze and fit them. Yellow-chromated couplings: Check that the gaps either side of the coupling halves are equal. TM02 0462 0000 Fig. 7 Gaps between coupling hal v es

chunks.heading: 4.3.3 Fitting the shaft seal, coupling and motor
chunks.text: Tighten the screws to the torque stated, see 2. Tightening torques and lubricants, and remove the adjusting fork. Check that the shaft rotates freely and noiselessly. Place the adjusting fork on the inside of one of the coupling guards. Fit the coupling guard (pos. 7) and the screws (pos. 7a). 12 / 20

chunks.heading: 4.4 Replacing the shaft seal of pumps with spacer coupling
chunks.text: 4.4 Replacing the shaft seal of pumps with spacer coupling

chunks.heading: 4.4.1 Dismantling
chunks.text: 4.4.1 Dismantling Remove the screws (pos. 7a) together with the coupling guards (pos. 7). Remove the screws (pos. 9) together with the coupling halves (pos. 10a) and the shaft pin (pos. 10). Slacken the three screws of the shaft seal (pos. 113) by approx. ¼ of a turn. Slacken the shaft seal (pos. 105) using the ring insert tool for shaft seal (pos. B) until the thread is completely free of the pump head. Pull the shaft seal off the shaft.

chunks.heading: 4.4.2 Assembly
chunks.text: 4.4.2 Assembly If necessary, clean and smooth the shaft end using the holder with emery cloth supplied with the shaft seal kit. Moisten the shaft end with soapy water. Press the shaft seal on the shaft, screw it into the pump head and tighten it with 35 Nm. Press the ring with the three hexagon socket set screws (pos. 113) against the hexagon plug. Tighten the screws (pos. 113) with 2.5 Nm. Lift the chamber stack by inserting a screwdriver or similar tool in the hole for the pin in the shaft and fit the adjusting fork, which is fitted to one of the coupling guards (pos. 7). TM02 7923 4403 Fig. 8 Fitting the adjusting fork Fit the pin (pos. 10) and the two coupling halves (pos. 10a). Lubricate and fit the four screws (pos. 9). Yellow-chromated couplings: Check that the gaps either side of the coupling halves are equal. TM02 0462 0000 Fig. 9 Gaps between coupling hal v es Tighten the screws to the torque stated, see 2. Tightening torques and lubricants, and remove the adjusting fork. Check that the shaft rotates freely and noiselessly. Place the adjusting fork on the inside of one of the coupling guards. Fit the coupling guard (pos. 7) and the screws (pos. 7a). 13 / 20

chunks.heading: 4.5 Checking and replacing impellers/wear rings and neck rings
chunks.text: 4.5 Checking and replacing impellers/wear rings and neck rings

chunks.heading: Impellers/wear rings
chunks.text: Impellers/wear rings Check if there is a noticeable groove in the impeller skirts (CR 10) or wear rings (CR 15 and 20) caused by friction (use a finger nail). If there is a groove, the impellers/wear rings must be replaced. The wear rings can be removed by means of the puller for neck ring (pos. C).

chunks.heading: Neck rings
chunks.text: Neck rings The neck rings (pos. 65) should always be replaced if the chamber stack has been dismantled. Push the retainer for neck ring free of the chamber using the puller for neck ring (pos. C). Remove the neck ring (pos. 45). Fit a new neck ring into the chamber. TM02 1182 0601 Fig. 10 Correct fitting of neck ring Press the retainer for neck ring down on the neck ring and make it engage with the chamber. It must be possible to move the neck ring freely (sideways) between the retainer and the chamber.

chunks.heading: Bearing rings
chunks.text: Bearing rings Check whether there is a visible or noticeable (use a finger nail) edge on the rotating bearing rings. The bearing rings (pos. 47a) and the chambers with bearing ring (pos. 4a) must be replaced at the same time. 14 / 20
